body.translated_text: The <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s> (law).
And the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) and <s>śīla</s> (conduct) of those who know it.
Transgression of <s>dharma</s> and reckless acts are observed [even] among the great ones,
due to the weakness of inferior [persons].
When there is a conflict of equal force, there is an option.
The <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is in the eighth [year].
In the ninth or the fifth, if desired.
The count of years [begins] from conception.
That [<s>upanayana</s>] is his second birth.
He from whom that [birth occurs] is the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).
And because of the teaching of the <s>Veda</s>.
In the eleventh and twelfth [years] for the <s>kṣatriya</s> and <s>vaiśya</s> [respectively].
Up to the sixteenth [year], the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (initiation verse) of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has not lapsed.
Up to the twenty-second [year] for a <s>rājanya</s> (kṣatriya).
Up to two more [i.e., the twenty-fourth year] for a <s>vaiśya</s>.
The girdles are of <s>muñja</s> grass, bowstring, and <s>maurvī</s> (hemp cord), in order.
The skins are of black antelope, <s>ruru</s> deer, and goat.
The garments for all are of <s>śāṇa</s> (hemp), <s>kṣauma</s> (linen), <s>cīra</s> (bark), and <s>kutapa</s> (wool).
And also cotton, undyed.
Dyed with saffron, according to some.
Of tree [bark] for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
Dyed with madder and turmeric for the other two.
The staffs for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> are of <s>bilva</s> or <s>palāśa</s> wood.
Of <s>aśvattha</s> or <s>pīlu</s> wood for the remaining [two varṇas].
Or of a tree fit for sacrifice, for all.
Undamaged, curved like a sacrificial post, with bark intact.
Reaching to the crown, forehead, or tip of the nose [respectively].
And [the hair may be] shaved, matted, with a topknot, or with braided locks.
One who holds an object in hand is <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (impure from eating); he should sip water without putting [the object] down.
Purification of objects: by wiping, heating, chipping, and washing for those of metal, stone, and those made of wood and horn.
For those of metal, as well as for [objects of] stone, gems, conch shells, and pearls.
For bone and earth, as for wood.
And for earth, by digging.
For cloth, rope, split bamboo, and leather, as for cloth.
Abandonment [is prescribed] for those completely ruined.
One should begin purification facing east or north.

body.text: śucau deśe āsīno dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ jānvantarākṛtvā yajñopavītyā maṇibandhanāt pāṇī prakṣālya vāgyatohṛdayaspṛśas triś catur vāpa ācāmed |
body.translated_text: Seated in a clean place, placing the right arm between the knees, wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavītī</s>), having washed both hands from the wrist, with speech restrained, touching the heart, one should sip water three or four times.
One wipes [the lips] twice.
And one should sprinkle the feet.
And one should touch the orifices of the head [i.e., eyes, ears, nostrils].
And one should place [water] on the crown of the head.
After sleeping, eating, and sneezing, [one should sip water] again.
When [food particles] are stuck between the teeth, [the purification is] as for teeth, except for scraping with the tongue.
Before they fall out, according to some.

body.text: cyuteśu āsrāvavad vidyān nigirann eva tac śuciḥ |
body.translated_text: When they have fallen out, one should know [the rule] as for discharge; swallowing them, one is indeed pure.

body.text: na mukhyā vipruṣa ucchiṣṭaṃ kurvanti na ced aṅgenipatanti |
body.translated_text: Drops [of saliva] from the mouth do not make [one] impure, provided they do not fall on a limb.
Purification from impure substances [is achieved] by removing the stain and smell.
That [is done] first with water and then with earth.
And in cases of contact with urine, feces, grease, blood, semen, and food.
And wherever the sacred tradition prescribes.

body.text: pāṇinā savyam upasaṅgṛhya anaṅguṣṭham adhīhi bho ity āmantrayed guruṃ |
body.translated_text: Grasping [the teacher's feet] with the left hand, without [using] the thumb, one should address the <s>guru</s> saying 'Teach, sir.'
Therein, the touching of the eyes, mind, and <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) [is done] with <s>darbha</s> grass.
The touching of <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) [is done] with <s>darbha</s> grass.
Three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls), each of fifteen <s>mātrās</s> (measures).
And one should sit on [<s>darbha</s> grass blades with] tips pointing east.
<s>Oṃ</s> [is recited] first; the five <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) end with '<s>satyam</s>' (truth).
Clasping the <s>guru</s>'s feet in the morning.
And at the beginning and end of <s>Veda</s> study.

body.text: anujñāta upaviśet prāṅmukho dakṣiṇataḥ śiṣya udaṅmukhovā |
body.translated_text: Having received permission, the student should sit down facing east, to the south [of the teacher], or facing north.
And the recitation of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
At the beginning, [reciting] '<s>Brahman</s>' at the commencement [of study].
The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> [is used] elsewhere also.
If there is an interruption, upon resumption, one should approach again.
After [the crossing of] a dog, a mongoose, a snake, a frog, or a cat — three days of fasting and absence [from study].
<s>Prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls) and the consumption of ghee for the others.
And the same [applies] for study at a cremation ground.
Before <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), one may act as one pleases, speak as one pleases, and eat as one pleases,
from what has not been offered [in sacrifice].
[After initiation, one becomes] a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student).
He should relieve himself as circumstances permit.
There is no rule of <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water) for him,
except for wiping, rinsing, and sprinkling.
There is no impurity from touching that [i.e., bodily excretions of a child before initiation].
But one should not employ him in offering oblations to fire or carrying <s>bali</s> (food offerings).
Nor should he utter a sacred <s>Vedic</s> formula, except for leading [the deceased] with <s>svadhā</s>.
The rules [begin] from <s>upanayana</s> onward.
The rules of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) have been stated.
Kindling the fire and going on the begging round.
Speaking the truth.
Touching water [for purification].
Some [say the rules begin] from the <s>godāna</s> (ceremony of shaving) onward.
And [he should] be outside during the twilight [prayers].

body.text: tiṣṭhet pūrvām āsītottarāṃ sajyotiṣyā jyotiṣodarśanād vāgyataḥ |
body.translated_text: He should stand during the morning <s>sandhyā</s> and sit during the evening one, with the [sacred] fire, until the stars are no longer visible, with speech restrained.
He should not gaze at the sun.

He should avoid honey, meat, perfumes, garlands, sleeping during the day, anointing, riding vehicles, wearing shoes, using an umbrella, desire, anger, greed, delusion, [musical] discourse, playing instruments, bathing [for pleasure], cleaning teeth, mirth, dancing, singing, slander, and fear.
In the presence of the <s>guru</s>: covering the throat, crossing the legs, reclining, and stretching out the feet.
Spitting, laughing, yawning, and cracking the fingers.
Looking at or touching a woman, when there is suspicion of sexual misconduct.
Gambling, association with low persons, taking what is not given, and violence.
The names of the <s>ācārya</s>, his wife, and the initiated.
[He should use only] auspicious words.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should always [avoid] liquor.
[The student should] sleep on the ground, sit low, rise before [the teacher], and go to bed after [him].
Restrained in speech, arms, and stomach.
He should not mention the <s>guru</s>'s name and lineage in his presence as though [they were] equal.
And the same when [the guru] is honored or in the presence of a superior.
Leaving aside [his own] bed, seat, and place, [he should offer] a reply [to the guru's call].
Approaching [the guru] at his word, without being seen [beforehand].
Seated in a lower place, he should rise when [there is] a crosswind or when the <s>guru</s> is seen.
He should follow [the guru] when he walks.
He should announce the work after being informed.
When called, he should be studying.
He should be devoted to what is agreeable and beneficial [to the guru].
And the same toward [the guru's] wife and sons.
He should not [perform for them]: eating leftovers, bathing, adorning, washing the feet, massaging, and embracing.
Embracing the <s>guru</s>'s wives upon returning from a journey.
Not with young women, according to some — as established by convention.
The begging round should be from all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), except from those accused and fallen.
The word '<s>bhavat</s>' (sir/madam) should be used at the beginning, middle, and end, in the order of <s>varṇas</s>.
Among the <s>ācārya</s>, relatives, and <s>gurus</s>; when [food is] not obtained, from others.
One should avoid the first [mentioned] before the latter ones.
Having informed the <s>guru</s> and received permission, one should eat.
In the <s>guru</s>'s absence, [one should inform] his wife, son, or fellow student.
With speech restrained, eating until satisfied but not greedily, having placed water nearby.
The discipline of students [is enforced] with a penalty.
When unable [to enforce otherwise], with a thin rope or split bamboo.
One who strikes with another [instrument] should be punished by the king.
One should observe <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) for twelve years in one <s>Veda</s>.
Or twelve [years] each for all [the Vedas].
Or until the [texts] are mastered.
At the end of study, the <s>guru</s> should be invited with a gift.
Or the bath [marking the end of studentship] is for one who has [already] made [the gift] and received permission.
The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) is the foremost among <s>gurus</s>.
The mother, according to some.
Some speak of a choice of <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) for him [who has completed his studies].
<s>Brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder), <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant), <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest hermit).
Of these, the householder is the source, because the others do not produce offspring.
Therein, the [rules for] the <s>brahmacārin</s> have been stated.
Being under the <s>ācārya</s>'s authority until the end [of study].
After the <s>guru</s>'s [duties], one should recite with the remainder of [one's] work.
In the absence of the <s>guru</s>, one should conduct oneself [as if serving] his offspring.
In their absence, [one should serve] an elder fellow student, or [tend] the fire.
One who conducts himself thus, with senses controlled, attains the world of <s>Brahman</s>.
And for the subsequent [<s>āśramas</s>], that which is not contrary to this [applies].
The <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) has no possessions.
He is <s>ūrdhvaretās</s> (one whose vital energy flows upward, i.e., celibate).
Of steady conduct during the rainy seasons.
Seeking alms, he should go to the village.
He should take the least, without turning back.
Free from expectation of blessings.
Restrained in speech, sight, and action.
He should wear a garment for the purpose of covering the loincloth.
A discarded [garment], according to some, after washing it.
He should not take a part of herbs or trees that has not been detached [naturally].

body.text: na dvitīyām apartu rātriṃ grāme vaset |
body.translated_text: He should not stay a second night in a village, except during the rainy season.
Shaven-headed or with a topknot.
He should avoid the destruction of seeds.
Impartial toward beings with respect to harm and kindness.
Without undertaking [worldly] enterprises.
The <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest hermit), living in the forest, eating roots and fruits, devoted to austerity.
Having established the [sacred] fire with the <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> [ceremony].
Not eating food from the village.
A worshiper of gods, ancestors, humans, beings, and sages.
Hospitable to all, except what is prohibited.
He may also use produce [from the wild].
He should not tread on ploughed land.
And he should not enter the village.
With matted hair, wearing bark and skins.
He should not eat [stored food] beyond one year.
However, the teachers [hold] that there is [only] one <s>āśrama</s>, because of the direct injunction for the householder's [stage].
The householder should marry a woman of equal [<s>varṇa</s>], not previously [married to] another, and not a <s>sapinda</s> (close relative).
Marriage [should be] with those of different <s>pravara</s> (ancestral lineage).
Beyond the seventh [generation] from paternal relatives.
And from those who share a common ancestor.
Beyond the fifth from maternal relatives.
In the <s>brāhma</s> [form of marriage], one should give [the bride], adorned and clothed, to one endowed with learning, conduct, kinship, and character.

body.text: saṃyogamantraḥ prājāpatye saha dharmaś caryatām iti |
body.translated_text: The formula of union in the <s>prājāpatya</s> [marriage] is: 'Let <s>dharma</s> (duty) be practiced together.'
In the <s>ārṣa</s> [marriage], one should give a pair of cattle to the father of the bride.
The <s>daiva</s> [marriage is] giving [the bride], adorned, to the officiating priest within the sacrificial enclosure.
The willing union by herself is the <s>gāndharva</s> [marriage].
The <s>āsura</s> [marriage] is the payment of wealth to the bride's relatives.
The <s>rākṣasa</s> [marriage] is by forcible seizure.
The <s>paiśāca</s> [marriage] is by approaching [a woman] without her knowledge.
The first four are lawful.
Six, according to some.

In <s>anuloma</s> (hypergamous) unions — with women one, two, or three <s>varṇas</s> below — the known [offspring] are: <s>savarṇa</s>, <s>ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>ugra</s>, <s>niṣāda</s>, <s>dauṣmanta</s>, and <s>pāraśava</s>.
The <s>pratiloma</s> (hypogamous) [offspring] are: <s>sūta</s>, <s>māgadha</s>, <s>āyogava</s>, <s>kṛtavaidehaka</s>, and <s>caṇḍāla</s>.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman begets sons from [men of] the [four] <s>varṇas</s> in order: <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>māgadha</s>, and <s>caṇḍāla</s>.
From those same [four varṇas], a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman [begets]: <s>mūrdhāvasikta</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>dhīvara</s>, and <s>pulkasa</s>.
From those same, a <s>vaiśya</s> woman [begets]: <s>bhṛjjakaṇṭha</s>, <s>māhiṣya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>vaideha</s>.
And a <s>śūdra</s> woman [begets]: <s>pāraśava</s>, <s>yavana</s>, <s>karaṇa</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>, according to some.
Passage to another <s>varṇa</s>, through elevation or degradation, [occurs] in the seventh [generation],
or the fifth, according to the teachers.
And for those born from mixed unions.
The <s>pratiloma</s> (hypogamous offspring) are devoid of <s>dharma</s>.
And [those born] of a <s>śūdra</s> woman.
But from a <s>śūdra</s> with a woman of unequal [higher] <s>varṇa</s>, [the offspring has] the conduct of the fallen.
The lowest [born from <s>pratiloma</s> unions] is the most sinful.
Virtuous sons purify [the lineage].
Three generations from an <s>ārṣa</s> [marriage].
Ten from a <s>daiva</s> [marriage].
Also ten from a <s>prājāpatya</s> [marriage].

body.text: daśa pūrvān daśa parān ātmānaṃ cabrāhmīputro brāhmīputraḥ |
body.translated_text: The son of a <s>brāhmī</s> [marriage] purifies ten ancestors, ten descendants, and himself.
One should approach [one's wife] during her fertile season.
Or at all [permitted] times, except those that are prohibited.
A worshiper of gods, ancestors, humans, beings, and sages.
Constant in private recitation [of the <s>Veda</s>].
And water offerings to the ancestors.
Other [duties] according to one's ability.
The fire [is established] beginning with [the marriage of] the wife, or beginning with the inheritance of property.
In that [fire], the <s>gṛhya</s> (domestic) rites [are performed].
The sacrifices to gods, ancestors, and humans, recitation of the <s>Veda</s>, and the <s>bali</s> (food-offering) rite.

body.text: agnāv agnir dhanvantarir viśve devāḥ prajāpatiḥsviṣṭakṛd iti homaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>homa</s> (oblation) [is offered] in the fire to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanvantari</s>, the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods), <s>Prajāpati</s>, and <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
And to the deities of the directions, each in its own [direction].
At the doors, to the great ones.
To the household deities, upon entering.
To <s>Brahman</s>, in the center.
To the Waters, at the water jar.
To Space — in the atmosphere,
the <s>bali</s> (offering) should be cast upward.
And to the night-wanderers, in the evening.
After pronouncing a blessing, the gift of alms-food, preceded by water.
And the same for those who give lawfully.

The fruits [of giving] are equal, double, thousandfold, and infinite — to a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned in the Vedas), and one who has mastered the entire <s>Veda</s>, [respectively].

The distribution of goods outside the sacred enclosure [is prescribed] in [cases related to] the <s>guru</s>'s purpose, settling, medicine, livelihood, the destitute, one about to sacrifice, study, journeys, and the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice.
Prepared food for those begging; uncooked for the others.
Even having promised, one should not give to one connected with <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
The words of one who is angry, elated, frightened, distressed, greedy, a child, an old man, confused, intoxicated, or insane — [these] untruths are not [counted as] sins.
One should feed first the guest, boys, the sick, pregnant women, women of the household, and the elderly — the lowest [in priority being served] last.
The cooking should be done after informing the <s>ācārya</s>, father, and friends.
The <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture reception) [is offered] upon the arrival of a <s>ṛtvik</s> (officiating priest), <s>ācārya</s>, father-in-law, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle.
[It is offered] again after one year.
Before [the interval], on [the occasions of] a sacrifice or a wedding.
And for a king and a <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar).
For a non-<s>śrotriya</s>, [only] a seat and water.

body.text: śrotriyasya tu pādyam arghyam annaviśeṣāṃś caprakārayet |
body.translated_text: But for a <s>śrotriya</s>, one should offer water for the feet, the <s>arghya</s> (respectful offering), and special foods.
Or always, distinguished by [special] preparation.
In the middle [rank], the gift of food to one not learned in the <s>Veda</s> but of virtuous conduct.
For those of the opposite [character]: grass, water, and ground [to sit on].
At the very least, a word of welcome.
And honor and regard.
Bed, seat, lodging, escorting, and attendance are the same for an equal or a superior.
Even a little, for an inferior.
A guest is one from a different village, staying for one night, who stands under the trees [awaiting the sun's] worship.
Inquiry about well-being, health, and freedom from disease.
For a <s>śūdra</s>, the last [greeting only].
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> is not a [proper] guest.
Except when he is employed in a sacrifice.
But a <s>kṣatriya</s>'s meal [is given] after the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Others [should be fed] together with the servants, for the sake of kindness.
Grasping the feet [of the teacher is done] daily when they meet.
But [also] upon arriving after [the teacher has been] away.
[This applies] for one's mother, father, their relatives, elder [brothers], learning-teachers, and their teachers.
When [two such persons] meet, [the greeting is given] to the superior.
Announcing one's own name, [saying] 'I am so-and-so, sir' — this is the <s>abhivāda</s> (salutation), when meeting those who are to be saluted.
Some [say] there is no restriction [on the formula] based on the gender combination in the salutation.
[One does] not [greet by grasping the feet], except after absence, in the case of women other than mother, father's wife, [elder] sister.
No grasping of the feet [is done] for brothers' wives or sisters.
But for younger <s>ṛtvij</s> (officiating priests), fathers-in-law, paternal uncles, and maternal uncles — [one should perform] rising and salutation.
Likewise, any other senior [person], a townsman of eighty or less [years of age], and even a <s>śūdra</s> equal in age to one's children [is to be greeted].
Even a junior <s>ārya</s> (noble person) [is greeted] by a <s>śūdra</s>.
Or one should avoid [calling] his name.
And [the brahmin] should be an unreciting servant of the king.

body.text: bho bhavann iti vayasyaḥ samāne 'hani jātaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Bho</s>' and '<s>Bhavan</s>' [are the forms of address] for a companion born on the same day.
A townsman [who is] senior by ten years [is to be treated as an elder].
One proficient in arts, by five [years].
A <s>śrotriya</s> (learned in the <s>Vedas</s>) and a <s>cāraṇa</s> (wandering scholar), by three.
[Those engaged in] <s>kṣatriya</s> and <s>vaiśya</s> occupations [but] devoid of learning.
And one who is consecrated [for a sacrifice], until the purchase [of <s>Soma</s>].
Wealth, kinship, [ritual] action, birth, and learning — these are to be honored, each later one being more powerful.
But sacred learning is the most weighty of all,
Because it is the root of <s>dharma</s>,
And of [the authority of] scripture.

Giving way on the road [is due] to one in a wheeled vehicle, one on the tenth day [after a birth], a <s>sthānu</s> (pillar-like ascetic), a pregnant woman, a bride, a recently-bathed [graduate], and a king.
But by the king, to a <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar) and to [another] <s>śrotriya</s>.
In times of emergency, a brahmin may use learning [acquired] from a non-brahmin.
[This involves] following [the teacher] and serving [him].
Upon completion [of studies], the brahmin is the teacher.
Officiating at sacrifices, teaching, and receiving gifts — [these are the livelihood] of all [twice-born].
The earlier [mentioned] is the superior teacher.
In the absence of that [livelihood], the <s>kṣatriya</s> mode of life [is permissible].
In the absence of that, the <s>vaiśya</s> mode of life.
[But certain things are] not to be traded by him.
Perfumes, [cooked] juices, prepared food, sesame, <s>śāṇa</s> (hemp), linen, and skins.
[And] dyed and bleached garments.
Milk and its products.
Roots, fruits, flowers, medicines, honey, meat, grass, and water are not prohibited [for trade].
And animals, when not connected with violence [in selling them for slaughter].
And [the trade in] men, women, and young children is always [prohibited].
Some [also prohibit trade in] land, rice, barley, goats, sheep, horses, bulls, cows, and oxen.
But there is a restriction —
[Namely, the exchange] of liquids for liquids,
And of animals [for animals].
Not in the case of salt and prepared food.
And of sesame.
But [exchange] of cooked [food] for an equal [measure] of the same [kind] is [permitted] when there is a [current] need.
In the case of inability [to earn a living], any livelihood [is permissible] except that of a <s>śūdra</s>.
Some [say] even that [is permissible] when life is in danger.
But the restriction regarding that [is] the avoidance of [inter-]<s>varṇa</s> mixing and eating forbidden food.
When life is in danger, even a brahmin may take up weapons.
A <s>kṣatriya</s> [may take up] the occupation of a <s>vaiśya</s>.

body.text: dvau loke dhṛtavratau rājā brāhmaṇaś ca bahuśrutaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Two in the world are [truly] firm in their vows: the king and the learned brahmin.'
'The life of the four classes of human beings — [all that which is characterized by] internal consciousness, movement, falling, and crawling — depends upon those two.'
'Production, protection, and non-confusion [of the classes] — that is <s>dharma</s>.'
'He alone is truly learned'
'Who knows the [ways of the] world, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (auxiliary sciences),
Who is skilled in debate, <s>Itihāsa</s> (history), and <s>Purāṇa</s> (ancient lore),'
Who is attentive to that [learning] and whose conduct accords with it.
One who is refined by the forty <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments),
Who delights in [the performance of] three [types of] rites,
Or six,
Who is well-trained in conventional and customary practices,
Who is to be exempted by the king from six [penalties] —

body.text: avadhyaś cābandhyaś cādaṇḍyaś cābahiṣkāryaścāparivādyaś cāparihāryaś ceti |
body.translated_text: He is not to be killed, not to be imprisoned, not to be fined, not to be banished, not to be reproached, and not to be deprived [of his possessions].

[The sacraments are:] <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite), <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for a male child), <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the hair), <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite), <s>nāmakaraṇa</s> (naming ceremony), <s>annaprāśana</s> (first feeding), <s>caula</s> (tonsure), and <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread ceremony).
Four Vedic observances (<s>vratāni</s>),
<s>Snāna</s> (the ritual bath at graduation), and the union with a wife (<s>sahadharmacāriṇī</s>).
The performance of the five [great] sacrifices — to the gods, ancestors, human beings, [all] beings, and brahmins.
And of these [further rites]:

body.text: aṣṭakā pārvaṇaḥ śrāddham śrāvaṇyāgrahāyaṇīcaitryāśvayujīti sapta pākayajñasamsthāḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, the <s>Pārvaṇa</s> (ancestral offering), the <s>Śrāddha</s> (funeral offering), the <s>Śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s>, <s>Caitrī</s>, and <s>Āśvayujī</s> — these are the seven forms of <s>pākayajña</s> (cooked-food sacrifices).

body.text: agnyādheyam agnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsāvāgrayaṇaṃ cāturmāsyāni nirūḍhapaśubandhaḥ sautrāmaṇīti saptahaviryajñasamsthāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Agnyādheya</s> (establishment of the sacred fires), <s>Agnihotra</s> (daily fire oblation), <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon sacrifices), <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering), <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal sacrifices), <s>Nirūḍhapaśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice), and <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> — these are the seven forms of <s>haviryajña</s> (oblation sacrifices).

body.text: agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśīvājapeyo 'tirātro 'ptoryāma iti sapta somasaṃsthāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Atyagniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, <s>Vājapeya</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, and <s>Aptoryāma</s> — these are the seven forms of <s>Somasaṃsthā</s> (<s>Soma</s> sacrifice).
These are the forty <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments).
Now, the eight qualities of the self:

body.text: dayā sarvabhūteṣu kṣāntir anasūyā śaucam anāyāsomaṅgalam akārpaṇyam aspṛheti |
body.translated_text: Compassion toward all beings, patience, freedom from envy, purity, equanimity, auspiciousness, freedom from meanness, and freedom from covetousness.

body.text: yasyaite catvāriṃśatsaṃskārā na cāṣṭāv ātmaguṇāna sa brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ sālokyaṃ gacchati |
body.translated_text: One who has [performed] the forty <s>saṃskāras</s> but does not have the eight qualities of the self — he does not attain union with <s>Brahman</s> or residence in [the world of] <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: yasya tu khalu saṃskārāṇām ekadeśo 'py aṣṭāv ātmaguṇā atha sa brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ sālokyaṃ cagacchati |
body.translated_text: But one who has even a portion of the <s>saṃskāras</s> [yet possesses] the eight qualities of the self — he indeed attains union with <s>Brahman</s> and residence in [the world of] <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: sa vidhipūrvakaṃ snātvā bhāryām adhigamyayathoktān gṛhasthadharmān prayuñjāna imāni vratāny anukarṣet |
body.translated_text: He, having bathed [at graduation] according to the prescribed rite, having taken a wife, and practicing the duties of a householder as declared, should observe these vows.
[He is] a <s>snātaka</s> (graduated student).
Always pure, fragrant, accustomed to bathing.
When he has the means, he should not wear worn-out or soiled garments.

body.text: na raktam ulbaṇam anyadhṛtaṃ vāso bibhṛyāt |
body.translated_text: He should not wear a garment that is excessively dyed, or one worn by another.
Nor [should he wear] garlands or sandals.
[He should wear garments that are] washed clean; in case of inability, [at least] bleached.
He should not let his beard grow without reason.
He should not carry fire and water simultaneously.
He should not drink from his cupped palms.
He should not sip water (<s>ācamana</s>) while standing, with water drawn up [in a vessel].
Not [with water poured] by a <s>śūdra</s>, an impure person, or with one hand.

body.text: na vāyvagniviprādityāpo devatā gāś ca pratipaśyan vā mūtrapurīṣāmedhyān vyudasyet |
body.translated_text: He should not void urine or excrement or impure [substances] while looking at wind, fire, a brahmin, the sun, water, deities, or cows.
He should not stretch out his feet toward these deities.
He should not clean away urine or excrement with leaves, clods, or stones.
He should not step on ashes, hair, nails, husks, potsherds, or impure [substances].
He should not converse with <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians), impure persons, or the unrighteous.
Having conversed [with such], he should mentally meditate on meritorious [persons].
Or converse with a brahmin.
He should call a barren [cow] 'one about to become a milk-cow.'
An inauspicious [thing], 'auspicious.'
A skull, '<s>bhagāla</s>' [a euphemism].
A rainbow, '<s>maṇidhanu</s>' (jewel-bow).
He should not point out to another a cow that is suckling.
Nor should he prevent her [from suckling].

body.text: na mithunī bhūtvā śaucaṃ prati vilambeta |
body.translated_text: After sexual intercourse, he should not delay in purifying himself.

body.text: na ca tasmin śayane svādhyāyam adhīyīta |
body.translated_text: And he should not study the <s>Veda</s> on that bed.
And having studied in the last watch of the night, he should not go back to sleep.
He should not enjoy an unadorned woman.
Nor a menstruating woman.
Nor should he embrace her.
Nor an unmarried girl.

He should avoid: [sitting] facing the [sacred] fire, blowing [the fire], argumentation, wearing garlands and perfumes outside [the house], [using another's] comb, eating together with his wife, looking into a well, entering through a back door, washing one foot with the other, sitting on a chair while eating, crossing a river by [swimming with] arms, and climbing or descending from trees or uneven [terrain], and [excessive] exertion of breath.
He should not board a doubtful [i.e., unsafe] boat.
He should protect himself in every way.
He should not walk about during the day with his head covered.
[But] covered at night.
And when voiding urine or excrement.
Not on the bare ground without covering [it first].
Nor far from a dwelling.
Not on ashes, cow-dung fuel, ploughed [ground], shade, paths, or places of pleasure.

body.text: ubhe mūtrapurīṣe tu divā kuryād udaṅmukhaḥ |
body.translated_text: He should void both urine and excrement during the day facing north.
And at the twilight times.
At night, facing south.

body.text: pālāśam āsanaṃ pāduke dantadhāvanam iti ca varjayet |
body.translated_text: He should avoid a seat of <s>palāśa</s> (butea) [leaves], shoes, and a tooth-cleaning [stick of palāśa].
And on a staircase, he should avoid [offering a] seat, salutation, and obeisance.
He should not let the forenoon, midday, and afternoon pass fruitlessly; according to his capacity, [he should devote them] to <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure).
But among these, <s>dharma</s> should be predominant.
He should not look at another's wife when she is naked.
He should not drag a seat with his foot.
He should not indulge in restlessness of the genitals, belly, hands, feet, speech, or eyes.
He should not cut, break, scratch, rub, or crack [the joints of his body] without reason.
He should not step over a calf's rope.
He should not be one who frequents [other people's] houses.
He should not go to a sacrifice [if] uninvited.
But merely for viewing, [he may go] as he wishes.
He should not eat food [placed] in his lap.
Nor [food] brought [by a servant] at night.
He should not eat [food] whose potency has been removed — such as that from which the oil has been extracted, whey, oil-cake, buttermilk, and the like.

body.text: sāyaṃprātas tv annam abhipūjitam anindan bhuñjīta |
body.translated_text: But at evening and morning, he should eat food that is honored [i.e., properly prepared], without criticizing [it].
He should never sleep naked at night.
Or bathe [naked].

body.text: yac cātmavanto vṛddhāḥ samyagvinītādambhalobhamohaviyuktā vedavida ācakṣate tat samācaret |
body.translated_text: And whatever self-controlled elders, well-disciplined, free from pride, greed, and delusion, and versed in the <s>Vedas</s>, declare — that he should follow.
For the sake of welfare and prosperity, he should approach the lord (<s>Īśvara</s>).
Not anyone else, except gods, teachers, and the righteous.

He should strive to dwell in an abode that is well-supplied with fuel, water, fodder, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and garlands; that has an exit; that is frequented mainly by noble people; that is not lazy [i.e., productive]; that is prosperous; and that is governed by the righteous.
He should circumambulate auspicious [objects], temples of deities, and quadrupeds, keeping them to his right.

body.text: manasā vā tatsamagram ācāram anupālayed āpatkalpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Or he may observe the entire code of conduct mentally, in times of emergency.
[He should be] devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s>.
[Living by] noble conduct.
A teacher of the learned.
Disciplined in purity.
He should be devoted to [Vedic] scripture.
Always non-violent, gentle, firm in action, given to self-control and generosity.

body.text: evam ācāro mātāpitarau pūrvāparāṃś ca sambandhānduritebhyo mokṣayiṣyan snātakaḥ śaśvadbrahmalokān na cyavate na cyavate |
body.translated_text: The <s>snātaka</s> (graduate) who conducts himself thus, freeing his mother, father, and earlier and later relatives from sin, never falls from the worlds of <s>Brahman</s> — never falls.
[The duties] of the twice-born are study, sacrifice, and giving.
For the brahmin, additionally: teaching, officiating at sacrifices, and receiving gifts.
But there is a restriction regarding the earlier [mentioned duties, i.e., they are primary].

Giving of [one's] <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) [is appropriate] in the case of [the needs of one's] teacher, kinsmen, dear ones, the teacher's [family], wealth, and learning — except as [otherwise] prescribed.
Agriculture and trade [are permissible] when not performed by oneself [i.e., through servants].
And money-lending.
The king has the additional [duty of] protection of all beings.
[He should exercise] just punishment.
He should support brahmins who are learned in the <s>Vedas</s>.
And brahmins who are without means.
And [keep them] free from taxes.
And those who are rendering service [as students].
And [he should have] readiness for conquest.
Especially in [times of] danger.
And [his] conduct [should be exercised] with chariot and bow.
Steadfastness in battle and never retreating.
There is no fault in killing in battle,

Except [in killing] one who is otherwise [i.e., not fighting], a charioteer, one who has surrendered, one who is weaponless, one with palms joined [in supplication], one with disheveled hair, one who has turned away, one who is seated, one who has climbed a bank or a tree, a messenger, a cow, a brahmin, or one who pleads.

body.text: kṣatriyaś ced anyas tam upajīvet tadvṛttyā |
body.translated_text: If a <s>kṣatriya</s> other [than the king] depends on him, [he should live] by the <s>kṣatriya</s> mode of life.
The conqueror should obtain the wealth [won] in battle.
But the vehicles [belong] to the king.
And the king takes the first share in a joint victory.
But the rest the king should distribute according to merit.

body.text: rājño balidānaṃ karṣakairdaśamam aṣṭamaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vā |
body.translated_text: The tax paid by cultivators to the king is one-tenth, one-eighth, or one-sixth.
Some [say] one-fiftieth of cattle and gold.
One-twentieth is the customs duty on merchandise.
One-sixth [is the tax] on roots, fruits, flowers, medicines, honey, meat, grass, and firewood.
Because [the king's] duty is to protect those [people].
And he should be constantly engaged in those [duties].
[His own] livelihood [comes] from the surplus.

body.text: śilpino māsi māsy ekaikaṃ karma kuryuḥ |
body.translated_text: Artisans should perform one work [for the king] each month.
By this, those who live by their own [crafts] are explained.
And boatmen and chariot-owners.
He should give them food.
Goods should be given by merchants [to the king] at cost price.
Found [property] without an owner — they should report [it] to the king.
Having publicized [it], the king should protect [it] for a year.
After [that period], the finder [takes] one-fourth, [and] the rest [goes to] the king.
Ownership [arises] through inheritance, purchase, partition, appropriation, and finding.
For a brahmin, additionally [there is] what is received [as a gift].
For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, what is conquered.
What is earned [through labor belongs] to the <s>vaiśya</s> and <s>śūdra</s>.
A discovered treasure is the king's property.
[Unless it belongs to] a brahmin of distinguished [learning].
Some [say] even a non-brahmin who reports [a treasure] should receive one-sixth.
Property stolen by thieves, when recovered, should be returned to its [rightful] place.
Or [the king] should give [compensation] from the treasury.
The property of a minor should be protected until [he] reaches the age of legal competence.
Or until the completion of [his Vedic] studies.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, additionally: agriculture, trade, animal husbandry, and money-lending.
The <s>śūdra</s> is the fourth <s>varṇa</s> (class), [with] one birth [only].
For him too: truthfulness, freedom from anger, and purity.
Some [say his] <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping) [consists merely of] washing the hands and feet.
[He may perform] the <s>śrāddha</s> (funeral) rite.
Maintenance of dependents.
Fidelity to his own wife.
And service to the higher [<s>varṇas</s>].
He should seek his livelihood from them.
Among those, he should serve the earlier [i.e., higher <s>varṇa</s>] first.
[He may receive their] worn-out shoes, umbrellas, garments, brooms, and the like.
Eating of leftover food.
And livelihood through craftsmanship.

body.text: yaṃ cāryam āśrayed bhartavyas tena kṣīṇo 'pi |
body.translated_text: Whatever noble [person] he takes refuge in — he should be maintained by that [person] even when impoverished.
And through him [the <s>śūdra</s>] is elevated.
His accumulation [of wealth] should be for the sake of that [master].
His salutation-<s>mantra</s> is permitted [only] with authorization.
Some [say] he may sacrifice by himself with <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked-food sacrifices).
And all [<s>varṇas</s>] should serve each successively higher one.
In the transgression of [duties between] an <s>ārya</s> (noble) and a non-<s>ārya</s>, there is equality in [the karmic consequence of] the action.
The king is [the authority] over all in what is desired, except for brahmins.
[He should be] one who does good and speaks well.
He should be well-trained in the three <s>Vedas</s> or in <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (logic/philosophy).
He should be pure, with senses controlled, endowed with virtuous companions and resourceful means.
He should be impartial toward his subjects.
He should act for their welfare.
While he sits on a higher seat, others except <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should sit below him.
They too should respect him.
He should duly protect the <s>varṇas</s> (social orders) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life).
And those who deviate, he should restore to their own <s>dharma</s> (duty).
For he becomes a sharer in the merit of <s>dharma</s>.
He should place foremost a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with learning, noble birth, eloquence, beauty, age, and good conduct, who is righteous in behavior and ascetic.
Under his guidance he should perform his duties.

body.text: brahmaprasūtaṃ hi kṣattram ṛdhyate na vyathata iti cavijñāyate |
body.translated_text: For it is known that the <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power) guided by <s>brahman</s> (priestly authority) prospers and does not suffer.
And whatever the interpreters of divine portents declare, he should heed.

body.text: tadadhīnam api hy eke yogakṣemaṃ pratijānate |
body.translated_text: For some maintain that welfare and security depend upon that.

In the <s>śālāgni</s> (household fire) he should perform rites conducive to prosperity combined with <s>śānti</s> (pacification), <s>puṇyāha</s> (auspicious day ceremonies), <s>svasti</s> (benediction), <s>ayana</s> (solstice rites), <s>āyuṣmat</s> (longevity rites), and <s>maṅgala</s> (auspicious ceremonies), as well as those involving <s>vidveṣaṇa</s> (creating enmity), <s>saṃvanana</s> (enchantment), <s>abhicāra</s> (sorcery), and the destruction of enemies.
The <s>ṛtvijas</s> (priests) should perform other rites as prescribed.

body.text: tasya ca vyavahāro vedo dharmaśāstrāṇy aṅgānyupavedāḥ purāṇam |
body.translated_text: His sources for legal proceedings are the <s>Veda</s>, the <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (law texts), the <s>aṅgas</s> (auxiliary sciences), the <s>upavedas</s> (secondary sciences), and the <s>purāṇas</s> (ancient lore).
The customs of region, caste, and family, when not contradicted by the sacred tradition, are also authoritative.
Farmers, merchants, cattle-rearers, money-lenders, and artisans — each within their own group.
Having ascertained the facts from them according to their respective authority, he should determine what is against <s>dharma</s>.
In ascertaining justice, reasoning is an auxiliary method.
Having deliberated by means of that, he should bring the matter to its proper conclusion.
In case of disagreement, having ascertained the facts from learned elders versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>, he should reach a conclusion.
For thus his highest good results.
It is known that <s>brahman</s> (priestly authority) united with <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power) sustains gods, ancestors, and humans.

body.text: daṇḍo damanād ity āhus tenādāntān damayet |
body.translated_text: They say <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment) derives from 'damana' (subduing); by means of it he should subdue the unruly.

body.text: varṇāśramāḥ svasvadharmaniṣṭhāḥ pretya karmaphalamanubhūya tataḥ śeṣena viśiṣṭadeśajātikularūpāyuḥśrutacitravittasukhamedhaso |
body.translated_text: The <s>varṇas</s> (social orders) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), steadfast in their own respective duties, after death having experienced the fruit of their actions, then by the remainder of merit are born with excellent region, caste, family, form, lifespan, learning, varied wealth, happiness, and intelligence.
They obtain birth accordingly.
Those who go astray and act contrarily are destroyed.
The instruction of the teacher and punishment protect them.
Therefore the king and the teacher should not be censured.

body.text: śūdro dvijātīn abhisaṃdhāyābhihatya cavāgdaṇḍapāruṣyābhyām aṅgamocyo yenopahanyāt |
body.translated_text: A <s>śūdra</s> who assails or strikes a member of the twice-born classes with verbal or physical violence shall have that limb cut off by which he offends.
For intercourse with a woman of the <s>ārya</s> (noble) class, the cutting off of the organ and confiscation of property.
If she was under protection, death as an additional penalty.
Now, if he listens to the <s>Veda</s>, his ears should be filled with molten tin or lac.
For reciting it, the tongue should be cut.
For memorizing it, the body should be split.
One who seeks equality in sitting, lying, or speech is to be punished.
A <s>kṣatriya</s> incurs a fine of one hundred for reviling a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
For physical violence, double.
A <s>vaiśya</s>, one and a half times.
But a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> incurs fifty for a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
Half that for a <s>vaiśya</s>.
Nothing for a <s>śūdra</s>.
Between a <s>kṣatriya</s> and a <s>vaiśya</s>, as between a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
The punishment for theft by a <s>śūdra</s> is eightfold.
For the others, it increases by double for each higher <s>varṇa</s>.
For the transgression of a learned person, the punishment is greater.
For taking fruits, vegetables, grain, or herbs, the fine is five <s>kṛṣṇalas</s> for a small amount.
When cattle are harmed, the fault lies with the owner.
But when a herdsman is involved, the fault lies with him.
On a road or in an unfenced field, the fault lies with the herdsman and the field-owner respectively.
Five <s>māṣas</s> for a cow.
Six for a camel or donkey.
Ten for a horse or buffalo.
Two each for goats and sheep.
For total destruction, one hundred.

body.text: śiṣṭākaraṇe pratiṣiddhasevāyāṃ ca nityaṃcailapiṇḍād ūrdhvaṃ svaharaṇam |
body.translated_text: For not performing prescribed duties and for engaging in forbidden activities, confiscation of property is always imposed, beyond the daily allowance of oil and food.

body.text: go'gnyarthe tṛṇamedhān vīrudvanaspatīnāṃ capuṣpāṇi svavad ādadīta phalāni cāparivṛtānām |
body.translated_text: For the sake of cows and fire, one may take grass, fuel, and flowers of creepers and trees as if they were one's own, and also fruits of unenclosed trees.
The lawful rate of interest on money-lending is twenty percent, that is, five <s>māṣas</s> per month.
Some say it should not exceed the amount for one year.
For long-standing loans, the principal may double.
A pledge that is being used does not bear interest.
Nor does that of one willing to pay or one who has been prevented from paying.
Interest in a cycle does not cease with time.
And there are also forced labor interest, bodily labor interest, and interest from the enjoyment of a pledged article.
In the case of cattle, water, wool, fields, one hundred, and vehicles, money-lending interest should not exceed fivefold the principal.
The property of one who is not mentally deficient, not a minor, enjoyed by others for ten years in the presence of the owner, belongs to the enjoyer.
But not when held by a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a renunciant, or a royal officer.
Cattle, land, and women cannot be lost through excessive use.
The heirs should discharge the debts.
Debts from suretyship, trade, bride-price, liquor, gambling, and fines should not devolve upon the sons.
Deposits, bailments, loans for use, and items not purchased as pledges are lost entirely without blame to any person through the owner's own fault.
A thief, with hair disheveled and carrying a pestle, should go to the king, confessing his deed.
He is purified by either execution or release.
A king who does not punish him becomes a sinner.
No corporal punishment shall be inflicted on a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
The penalties are: deprivation of livelihood, public proclamation, banishment, and branding.
If there is no reform, he shall undergo <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation).
An accomplice is equal to the thief when the act is deliberate.
Even the receiver of stolen property, if connected with the wrongdoing.
Punishment should be determined based on knowledge of the person's strength, the offense, and the consequences.
Or acquittal, based on the pronouncement of an assembly of <s>Veda</s>-knowers.
In case of disagreement, the establishment of truth is by means of witnesses.

body.text: bahavaḥ syur aninditāḥ svakarmasu prātyayikā rājñāṃniṣprītyanabhitāpāś cānyatarasmin |
body.translated_text: They should be many, blameless, trustworthy in their own occupations, and free from partiality or hostility toward either party in the king's court.
Even <s>śūdras</s> may serve as witnesses.
But a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be compelled to testify by the word of a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>, if he is not bound by the case.
Those not assembled and not asked should not give testimony.
In failing to testify or in false testimony, they incur guilt.
Heaven is the reward for truthful testimony; for its opposite, hell.
Even those not bound by the case should speak when called upon.
Testimony given under duress has no binding force.
Nor that given by one who is intoxicated.
The guilt falls on the witnesses, assessors, the king, or the judge when <s>dharma</s> procedure is violated.
Some hold that truth may be established by an oath.
That oath should be taken in the presence of gods, the king, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, for non-<s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
A witness lying about small cattle destroys ten people.
For cows, horses, humans, and land, ten times more for each.
Or everything in the case of land.
For theft, the result is hell.
For water, the same as for land.
And in the case of sexual union.
For honey and ghee, the same as for cattle.
For cloth, gold, grain, and sacred knowledge, the same as for a cow.
For vehicles, the same as for a horse.
A witness who speaks falsely shall be banished and fined.
There is no fault in untruthful speech if a life depends upon it.
But not for preserving the life of a wicked person.
The king, the chief judge, or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> learned in the <s>śāstras</s> may adjudicate.
He should oversee the chief judge.
He should wait one year when there is no clear evidence.
But in matters involving milch cows, draft oxen, women, and procreation, swiftly.
And in urgent cases.
In all matters of <s>dharma</s>, truthful speech in the court of justice is the most important.
The impurity from death lasts ten nights for <s>sapiṇḍa</s> (near) relatives of those who are not officiating priests, initiates, or <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate students).
Eleven nights for a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
Twelve nights for a <s>vaiśya</s>.
Half a month, according to some.
One month for a <s>śūdra</s>.

body.text: tac ced antaḥ punar āpatec cheṣeṇa śudhyeran |
body.translated_text: If within that period another death occurs, purification is completed with the remaining days.
If only a night remains, then with two days.
If at dawn, then with three days.
For those killed by cows or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, purification is immediate.
And for those killed by the king's wrath.
In battle.
And for those who die willingly by fasting, weapons, fire, poison, water, hanging, or falling.
The offering of the rice-ball ceases at the seventh or fifth generation.
The same applies at birth.
That applies to both mother and father.
Or to the mother alone.
For a miscarriage, the impurity lasts as many nights as the months of pregnancy.
Or three days.
And if heard of after the tenth day, one night.
For a non-<s>sapiṇḍa</s> relative by blood, and for a fellow student.
For a fellow <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), one day.
And for a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has completed his studies.
Upon touching a corpse, the impurity lasts ten nights if done intentionally.
The rule stated for <s>vaiśyas</s> and <s>śūdras</s> applies.
Or the period of menstruation.
And for the first two classes as well.
Or three days.
The same applies to the teacher, his son, his wife, the one who commissioned the sacrifice, and the pupil.

body.text: avaraś ced varṇaḥ pūrvavarṇam upaspṛśet pūrvovāvaraṃ tatra śavoktam āśaucam |
body.translated_text: If a lower <s>varṇa</s> touches a higher <s>varṇa</s>, or a higher one touches a lower, the impurity prescribed for a corpse applies.
Purification from contact with an outcast, a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, a woman in childbirth, a menstruating woman, a corpse, or one who has touched these, is by touching water while clothed.
And upon following a funeral procession.
And upon contact with a dog.
Some say, whatever it may pollute.
The water offering is made by <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives for one whose <s>cūḍā</s> (tonsure) ceremony has been performed.
And for their women.
Some say, for those who have been given in marriage.
All should be <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate), sleeping and sitting on the ground.
They should not anoint themselves.
They should not eat meat until the offering has been made.
The water-offering is performed on the first, third, seventh, and ninth days.
And the discarding of garments.
But at the end, for the lowest castes.
From the appearance of teeth onward, both parents observe the rites.
For children, those in a distant land, renunciants, and non-<s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives, purification is immediate.
And for kings, because it would conflict with their duties.
And for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, for the purpose of not interrupting <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic study).
Now regarding <s>śrāddha</s> (the rite for the deceased ancestors).
On the new-moon day he should offer to the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors).
Or from the fifth day onward of the dark fortnight.
According to his faith, at any time.
Or the time restriction applies when the requisite materials, place, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are available.
According to his ability, he should enhance the quality and preparation of the food.
He should feed nine or fewer, an odd number.
Or as many as he can.
They should be learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s> endowed with eloquence, beauty, age, and good conduct.
Gifts should be made first to young <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Some say, to those who are like fathers.
And he should not use the <s>śrāddha</s> for the purpose of cultivating friendships.

body.text: putrābhāve sapiṇḍā mātṛsapiṇḍāḥ śiṣyāś ca dadyuḥ |
body.translated_text: In the absence of a son, <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives, maternal <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives, or pupils should make the offerings.
In the absence of those, the officiating priest or teacher.

body.text: tilamāṣavrīhiyavodakadānair māsaṃ pitaraḥprīṇanti | matsyahariṇaruruśaśakūrmavarāhameṣamāṃsaiḥsaṃvatsarāṇi|gavyapayaḥpāyasair dvādaśa varṣāṇi|vārdhrīṇasenamāṃsena kālaśākacchāgalohakhaḍgamāṃsair madhumiśraiś cānantyam |
body.translated_text: With offerings of sesame, black beans, rice, barley, and water, the ancestors are gratified for one month; with the flesh of fish, deer, <s>ruru</s> deer, hare, tortoise, boar, and ram, for as many years; with cow's milk <s>pāyasa</s> (rice-pudding), for twelve years; and with the flesh of the <s>vārdhrīṇasa</s> (a large bull), <s>kālaśāka</s> (black vegetable), goat, red goat, and rhinoceros, mixed with honey, the gratification is eternal.

He should not feed a thief, a eunuch, an outcast, an atheist, one who lives like them, one who has killed a hero, the husband of a remarried woman, a village priest, a goat-herd, one who has abandoned his sacred fires, a drunkard, a deceiver, a false witness, or a professional conjurer.
Nor a paramour.
Nor one in whose household such a person resides.

Nor those who are: one who lives on the earnings of his daughter, one who sells <s>soma</s>, an arsonist, a poisoner, one who has broken his vow, a servant of a community, one who has gone to a forbidden woman, a violent person, one who has married before his elder brother, one who has married after his younger brother, one who has given his wife to another, one who has taken another's wife, one who has abandoned himself, one with bad nails, one with discolored teeth, one with white-spotted skin, the son of a remarried woman, a gambler, one defeated in dispute, a servant, one who acts the part of another, the husband of a <s>śūdra</s> woman, one dismissed from service, one with leprosy, a money-lender, a merchant, or one who lives by crafts, playing the lute, cymbals, dancing, or singing.
Nor those divided by their father unwillingly.
And some say pupils and those of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage) as well.
He should feed persons beyond the number of three.
One who is virtuous.

body.text: sadyaḥ śrāddhī śūdrātalpagas tatpurīṣe māsaṃnayati pitṛṛn |
body.translated_text: One who performs the <s>śrāddha</s> and on that same day sleeps with a <s>śūdra</s> woman consigns his ancestors to her excrement for a month.
Therefore on that day he should be a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate).
The <s>śrāddha</s> is spoiled by the sight of a dog, a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, or an outcast.
Therefore he should make the offering in an enclosed place.
Or he may scatter sesame seeds around.
Or a purifier of the row may rectify it.

body.text: paṅktipāvanaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavij jyeṣṭhasāmikas triṇāciketastrimadhus trisuparṇaḥ pañcāgniḥ snātako mantrabrāhmaṇavid dharmajñobrahmadeyānusaṃtāna iti |
body.translated_text: A purifier of the row is one who knows the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (auxiliary sciences), one who maintains the <s>jyeṣṭhasāma</s> fire, one who has thrice performed the <s>Nāciketa</s> rite, one who has thrice performed the <s>Trimedha</s> rite, one who has thrice performed the <s>Trisuparṇa</s> rite, one who maintains five fires, a <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic study), one who knows both <s>mantra</s> and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> portions, one who knows <s>dharma</s>, and one descended from a family that received a <s>brahmadeya</s> (gift of sacred learning).
The same applies for <s>havis</s> (oblation) offerings.
Those with bad nails and the like should be excluded from the <s>śrāddha</s> one by one.
And the same applies when the <s>śrāddha</s> is performed with uncooked food.

Beginning with <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> (July-August), having performed the <s>upākarma</s> (commencement ceremony) on the <s>Proṣṭhapadī</s> full-moon day, he should study the <s>Vedas</s> during the rainy season.
For four and a half months, or five months, or during the southern course of the sun.
A <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) who has let his hair grow should not eat meat.
Or the observance lasts two months.
One should not study when a dust-raising wind blows during the day.
Nor at night when it is audible to the ears.
Nor when there are sounds of arrows, drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (a type of drum), or cries of distress.
Nor when there is the howling of dogs, jackals, or donkeys.
Nor when there are meteors, rainbows, or mist.
Nor when clouds appear outside the rainy season.
Nor after urinating or defecating.
Nor at twilight or during the night at bodies of water.
Nor when it rains.
Some include the ant-hills in the list.
Nor while serving food to the teacher.
Nor during an eclipse.
Nor when frightened, riding a vehicle, lying down, or with feet stretched out.
Nor in a cremation ground, at the boundary of a village, on a highway, or in an impure place.
Nor in the presence of a foul smell, a corpse within sight, the announcement of a death, a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, or a <s>śūdra</s>.
Nor after eating or upon belching.
And when the sound of <s>Sāma</s> chanting is heard, one should not recite the <s>Ṛg</s> or <s>Yajur Veda</s>.
Unseasonable thunder, earthquakes, eclipses of <s>Rāhu</s>, and meteors are occasions for suspending study.
And when fires are produced by thunder, rain, and lightning;
during the day in the corresponding season;
in the case of lightning, at night and from the latter part of the night;
when it begins from the first third of the day onward, the entire [day is suspended];
a meteor is equivalent to lightning, according to some;
thunder [suspends study] in the afternoon;
and also at nightfall;
all [study is suspended] at night from midnight onward;
and during the day if there is [visible] lightning;
and when a king who rules the territory has died;
and when one who has been away meets another;
at a battle, the placing of the sacred fires, the completion of Vedic study, vomiting, <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites), and a sacrificial meal -- [study is suspended] for a day and a night;
and on the new moon day;
or for two days;
the full moon days of <s>Kārttika</s>, <s>Phālguna</s>, and <s>Āṣāḍha</s>;
the three <s>Aṣṭakā</s> days -- for three nights;
the last one only, according to some;
on both sides of the annual [Vedic recitation];
for all, when rain, lightning, and thunder occur simultaneously;
when it is drizzling;
after eating, at a festival;
and for four <s>muhūrtas</s> (time periods) at night after study;
always, according to some, when in a town;
even one who is mentally impure [should not study];
for those performing <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites), [the suspension is] without fixed time;
even when there is contact with one who has not prepared food for a <s>śrāddha</s>;
and those whom they remember for each branch of knowledge;
a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should eat [food prepared by] those twice-born who are commended and engaged in their own duties;
and he should accept [gifts from them];

Fuel, water, barley, grass, roots, fruits, honey, protection, [the use of] a bed, seat, shelter, conveyance, milk, curds, grain, small fish, millet, garlands, a path, and vegetables -- these may be accepted from all without being asked;
and other things [may be accepted from all] when maintaining ancestors, gods, a teacher, or dependents;
and [food may be taken] from a <s>Śūdra</s> if there is no other means of livelihood;
herdsmen, field-cultivators, those connected with one's family, employers, and personal servants -- their food may be eaten;
and a merchant who is not an artisan;
[the following] food should never be eaten:
that in which hair or insects have fallen;
that which has been touched by a menstruating woman, a black bird, or a foot;
that which has been looked at by an embryo-killer;
that which is spoiled in intent;
that which has been smelled by a cow;
that which has turned sour, and plain buttermilk without curds;
that which has been cooked again;
stale food -- except vegetables, preparations for chewing, oil, meat, and honey;

[food] of one who has been abandoned, a promiscuous woman, one falsely accused, one of bad repute, one undergoing punishment, a carpenter, a miser, a jailer, a physician, a deer-hunter, a distiller, a leftover-eater, a public feeder, and those who hate [Brahmins];
of those unfit to sit in a row [at a meal] -- as listed previously up to <s>Durvāla</s>;
[food given] without [proper] rice, without sipping water, and without rising [to receive the guest] -- these are to be avoided;
when an equal and an unequal are [dining together], an odd and an even [number], honor is given according to precedence;
and [food that is] unhonored [should not be eaten];
and the milk of a cow within ten days of calving, during impurity [from childbirth];
and [the milk] of a goat and a buffalo [under the same conditions];

body.text: nityam āvikam apeyam auṣṭram aikaśaphaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: sheep's milk, camel's milk, and that of one-hoofed animals should never be drunk;
and [the milk] of a cow that is constantly dripping, of one recently calved, and of one that is not joined [with a calf];
and of one whose calf is dead;
among five-clawed animals, the following are [permitted]: the hedgehog, hare, porcupine, monitor lizard, rhinoceros, and tortoise;
[the following are forbidden:] those with teeth on both jaws, hairy animals, one-hoofed animals, the <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow), the diving bird, the <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy shelduck), and the swan;
the crow, the heron, the vulture, the hawk, aquatic birds, those with red feet or beaks, the domestic fowl, and the pig;
and the milch cow and the draught ox;
meat of an animal that has died of disease, that has been newly killed, and meat [killed] in vain;
sprouts, confused [mixtures], garlic, and exudations;
red [varieties of] the <s>vraścana</s> (cutting plant);
the <s>nica</s>, the <s>dāru</s> (woodpecker), the crane, the egret, the parrot, the cormorant, the lapwing, the vulture, and nocturnal creatures are not to be eaten;
those that peck, scratch, and are web-footed may be eaten;
and fish that are not deformed;
and [animals] may be killed for the sake of <s>dharma</s> (religious duty);
one should eat [meat] that has been killed by a predator, that has no visible defect, that has been praised by word, and that has been sprinkled [with consecrated water];
a woman is not independent in matters of <s>dharma</s> (religious duty);
she should not transgress against her husband;
she should be restrained in speech, sight, and action;
a woman without a husband, desiring offspring, [may approach] her husband's brother (<s>devara</s>);
one who has been brought forth by an elder [brother's wife] should not pass beyond the [proper] season;
[she should approach one] from among those connected by <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral cake), <s>gotra</s> (lineage), or <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) -- or merely from the same origin;
not one who is not a brother-in-law (<s>devara</s>), according to some;
not beyond a second [child];
the child belongs to the begetter;
or to another, by agreement;
and [the child belongs to the owner] of the field, while [the husband] is alive;
from another man, [the child belongs] to that man;
or to both;
but because of the husband's protection, [the child belongs] to the husband alone;
when [the husband] is heard [to be alive], she should go to him;
but if he has gone forth as a renunciant, she is released because the connection [is dissolved];
twelve years [one should wait] for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is connected through learning;
and likewise, when an elder brother [has not yet married], the younger should [wait regarding] marriage, fire-rites, and taking a maiden;
six [years], according to some;

body.text: trīn kumāry ṛtūn atītya svayaṃyujyetāninditenotsṛjya pitryān alaṃkārān |
body.translated_text: after three seasons have passed, a maiden may unite herself with a man of good repute, setting aside her father's ornaments;
the giving [of a daughter in marriage should be] before puberty;
one who does not give [her in time] incurs blame;
before the appearance of the garment [i.e., menstruation], according to some;
accepting wealth for the purpose of accomplishing a marriage, and in the case of a connection for the preservation of <s>dharma</s>, [is permitted] from a <s>Śūdra</s>;
and from others as well, except a <s>Śūdra</s>, if he has many cattle but is of inferior conduct;
[from one with] a hundred cows, if he has not established the sacred fires;
and [from one with] a thousand cows, if he has not performed the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice;
and [the wealth] of the seventh [generation], if not consumed, for purposes that are not for accumulation;
even from those of inferior conduct;
he should declare [the truth] when questioned by the king;
for he [the king] must maintain one who is endowed with learning and good character;
if it is not done, it results in harm to the preservation of <s>dharma</s>;
thus have been described the duties of the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) and the duties of the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life);

body.text: atha khalv ayaṃ puruṣo yāpyena karmaṇā lipyate yathaitad ayājyayājanam abhakṣyabhakṣaṇam avadyavadanaṃśiṣṭasyākriyā pratiṣiddhasevanam iti |
body.translated_text: now, a person becomes tainted by censurable conduct, such as officiating at sacrifices for unworthy persons, eating forbidden food, speaking what is reprehensible, failing to perform what is prescribed, and engaging in prohibited activities;

body.text: tatra prāyaścittaṃ kuryāt na kuryād iti mīmāṃsante |
body.translated_text: regarding that, they deliberate: should one perform expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) or not?
'One should not perform it,' say some;
'for <s>karma</s> (action) is never exhausted,' [they argue];
'one should perform it,' say others;
for it is known that 'having sacrificed with the <s>Punaḥstoma</s> (re-pressing rite), one returns to the pressing [of Soma]';
and having sacrificed with the <s>Vrātyastoma</s> rites;

body.text: tarati sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ tarati brahmahatyāṃyo,aśvamedhena yajate |
body.translated_text: 'one who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) crosses over all sin, crosses over the sin of killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>';
and 'one should have a person accused [of a grave offense] sacrifice with the <s>Agniṣṭut</s>';

body.text: tasya niṣkrayaṇāni japas tapo homa upavāso dānam |
body.translated_text: the means of atonement for that are: recitation (<s>japa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), fire-offerings (<s>homa</s>), fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>), and gifts (<s>dāna</s>);

body.text: upaniṣado vedāntaḥ sarvacchandaḥsu saṃhitā madhūnyaghamarṣaṇam atharvaśiro rudrāḥ puruṣasūktaṃ rājatarauhine sāmanībṛhadrathantare puruṣagatir mahānāmnyo mahāvairājaṃ mahādivākīrtyaṃjyeṣṭhasāmnām anyatamad bahiṣpavamānaṃ kūṣmāṇḍāni pāvamānyaḥsāvitrī ceti pāvamānāni |
body.translated_text: the purificatory [texts] are: the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the <s>Vedānta</s>, the <s>Saṃhitā</s> in all meters, the <s>Madhu</s> [section], the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>, the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, the two <s>Rājatarauhiṇī</s> [sections], the <s>Sāmans</s>, the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>, the <s>Puruṣagati</s>, the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s>, the <s>Mahāvairāja</s>, the <s>Mahādivākīrtya</s>, any one of the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāmans</s>, the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>, the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, the <s>Pāvamānīs</s>, and the <s>Sāvitrī</s> -- these are the purificatory [recitations];

body.text: payovratatā śākabhakṣatā phalabhakṣatāprasṛtayāvako hiraṇyaprāśanaṃ ghṛtaprāśanaṃ somapānam itimedhyāni |
body.translated_text: the purifying [observances] of diet are: a milk diet, eating vegetables, eating fruits, subsistence on a handful of barley, eating gold [mixed with food], eating ghee, and drinking <s>Soma</s>;

body.text: sarve śiloccayāḥ sarvāḥ sravantyaḥ puṇyā hradāstīrthāny ṛṣinivāsā goṣṭhapariskandhā iti deśāḥ |
body.translated_text: the [purifying] places are: all mountain peaks, all flowing rivers, holy pools, pilgrimage sites, abodes of sages, and the precincts of cow-pens;
the austerities are: <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), truthful speech, touching water at the <s>savanas</s> (Soma pressings), wearing wet garments, sleeping on the ground, and fasting;

body.text: hiraṇyaṃ gaur vāso 'śvo bhūmis tilā ghṛtam annam itideyānīti |
body.translated_text: the things to be given are: gold, a cow, a garment, a horse, land, sesame, ghee, and food;

body.text: saṃvatsaraḥ ṣaṇmāsāś catvāras trayo vā dvauvaikaś caturviṃśatyaho dvādaśāhaḥ ṣaḍahas tryaho 'horātra itikālāḥ |
body.translated_text: the time periods [for penance] are: a year, six months, four or three months, two months, one month, twenty-four days, twelve days, six days, three days, and a day and night;
these same [penances], when there is no specific prescription, may be performed optionally;
for grave sins, grave [penances]; for light sins, light [penances];
the <s>Kṛcchra</s> (difficult penance), the <s>Atikṛcchra</s> (exceedingly difficult penance), and the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance) -- these are universal expiations;

body.text: tyajet pitaraṃ(pitṛ) rājaghātakaṃ śūdrayājakaṃśūdrārthayājakaṃ vedaviplāvakaṃ bhrūṇahanaṃ yaś cāntyāvasāyibhiḥsaha saṃvased antyāvasāyinyāṃ ca |
body.translated_text: one should abandon a father who is a regicide, who officiates at sacrifices for <s>Śūdras</s>, who sacrifices on behalf of <s>Śūdras</s>, who corrupts the <s>Vedas</s>, who kills an embryo, who lives with <s>Antyāvasāyins</s> (outcastes), or who cohabits with an outcaste woman;

body.text: tasya vidyāgurūn yonisaṃbandhāṃś ca saṃnipātyasarvāṇy udakādīni pretakāryāṇi kuryuḥ |
body.translated_text: his teachers of sacred knowledge and blood relations should be assembled, and they should perform all the funeral rites beginning with the offering of water, as for a dead person;
and they should turn his water vessel upside down;

body.text: dāsaḥ karmakaro vāvakarād amedhyapātram ānīyadāsīghaṭāt pūrayitvā dakṣiṇāmukho yadā viparyasyed amukam anudakaṃkaromi iti nāmagrāham |
body.translated_text: a slave or hired servant, having brought from a refuse heap a vessel for impure substances and filled it from a maidservant's pitcher, facing south, should pour it out [saying]: 'I make [so-and-so], naming the name, to be without water';
all should touch [the vessel] together, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, with hair loosened;
and the teachers of sacred knowledge and blood relations should observe [him];
after sipping water, they should enter the village;

body.text: ata uttaraṃ tena saṃbhāṣya tiṣṭhed ekarātraṃ japansāvitrīm ajñānapūrvam |
body.translated_text: after that, one who has spoken with him should stand for one night reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, if done unknowingly;
and for three nights if done knowingly;

body.text: yas tu prāyaścittena śudhyet tasmiñ śuddheśātakumbhamayaṃ pātraṃ puṇyatamād dhradāt pūrayitvā sravantībhyovā tata enam apa upasparśayeyuḥ |
body.translated_text: but for one who may be purified through expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) -- when he is purified, they should fill a golden vessel from the holiest pool or from flowing rivers, and then sprinkle him with water;

body.text: athāsmai tatpātram dadyus tatapratigṛhya japecśāntā dyauḥ śāntā pṛthivī śāntaṃ śivam antarikṣaṃ yo rocanastābhamam gṛhṇāmiiti |
body.translated_text: then they should give him that vessel; receiving it, he should recite: 'Peaceful is the sky, peaceful is the earth, peaceful and auspicious is the atmosphere; I take hold of this shining, radiant [vessel]';

body.text: etair yajurbhiḥ pāvamānībhis taratsamandībhiḥkūṣmāṇḍaiś cājyaṃ juhuyād |
body.translated_text: with these <s>Yajus</s> formulas, with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses, with the <s>Taratsamandī</s> hymns, and with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> mantras, he should offer ghee into the fire;
he should give gold to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
or a cow;
and to the teacher;

body.text: yasya tu prāṇāntikaṃ prāyaścittaṃ sa mṛtaḥśudhyet |
body.translated_text: but one whose expiation extends to the end of life is purified [only] at death;

body.text: sarvāṇy eva tasminn udakādīni pretakarmāṇi kuryuḥ |
body.translated_text: all funeral rites beginning with the offering of water should be performed for him;
this same purificatory water [ceremony applies] in all minor offenses;

those who have fallen are: the killer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the drinker of liquor, one who has sexual relations with the teacher's wife, one who approaches the wife of a mother's or father's relative, a thief, an atheist, one who habitually performs condemned acts, one who has been cast out but not undergone penance, and one who abandons one who has not fallen;
and those who associate with fallen persons;
and one who associates with them for a year;
the loss of the rites of the twice-born constitutes 'falling';
and likewise, failure [to attain merit] in the hereafter;
some call that 'hell';
the first three [offenses -- killing a Brahmin, liquor, teacher's wife] are beyond description, according to [the rule];
a man does not fall [for intercourse] with women, if it is not the teacher's wife, according to some;
a woman falls in the case of embryo-killing and intercourse with a man of lower <s>varṇa</s>;
perjury, betrayal of the king's trust, slander, and false accusation against one's teacher are equal to the great sins;

[eating the food] of those unfit to sit in a row at a meal, as listed earlier up to <s>Durvāla</s>, a cow-killer, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-killer, one who has done the same, one who has broken the vow of chastity, and one who has lost the <s>Sāvitrī</s> -- [eating their food] constitutes a minor offense;
through ignorance, [if one has] taught incorrectly, and [if] the <s>ṛtvij</s> (officiating priest) or <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) is one who should be fallen -- they are to be abandoned;
otherwise, if abandoned, one falls;
and the recipient of his gifts [also falls], according to some;
one should never withhold maintenance from one's mother and father;
but they should not share in the inheritance;
in falsely accusing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the guilt is equivalent [to the original offense];
twice [the guilt] when the offense is repeated;
and in causing harm to the weak, if one is capable of releasing [them];
reviling a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in anger results in exclusion from heaven for a hundred years;
in the case of a blow, a thousand [years];
in the case of drawing blood, [the exclusion lasts] for as many [years] as the grains of dust one would gather by running past the [spilled blood];
expiation [is prescribed for these];
for the killer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, casting oneself into fire three times, each time after being cut;
or one should become a target for armed warriors in battle;

body.text: khaṭvāṅgakapālapāṇir vā dvādaśa saṃvatsarānbrahmacārī bhaikṣāya grāmaṃ praviśet karmācakṣāṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: or, carrying a skull and a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-topped staff) in hand, living as a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) for twelve years, he should enter a village to beg, declaring his deed;
he should step off the path upon seeing a respectable person;
standing and sitting in the [proper] postures, touching water at the <s>savanas</s> (Soma pressings), he would be purified;
or [he is purified] if he saves the life of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in a [dangerous] situation;
in the case of diminished wealth, one who has made restitution at least threefold [is purified];
or at the final bath of an <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice);
or at another sacrifice, if it includes the <s>Agniṣṭut</s>;
if one is charged [with killing a Brahmana] but has not actually killed;
and likewise for [killing] an <s>Ātreyī</s> (woman of the Atri lineage);
and when the [caste of the] embryo is unknown;

body.text: rājanyavadhe ṣaḍvārṣikaṃ prākṛtaṃ brahmacaryamṛṣabhaikasahasrāś ca gā dadyāt |
body.translated_text: for killing a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, [one should perform] the ordinary <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate penance) for six years and give cows with one bull per thousand;

body.text: vaiśye tu traivārṣikam ṛṣabhaikaśatāś ca gādadyād |
body.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, three years, and he should give cows with one bull per hundred;

body.text: śūdre saṃvatsaram ṛṣabhaikādaśāś ca gā dadyāt |
body.translated_text: for a <s>Śūdra</s>, one year, and he should give cows with one bull per eleven;
and likewise for [killing] a non-<s>Ātreyī</s> woman;
and a cow, as for [killing] a <s>Vaiśya</s>;
and for killing a frog, mongoose, crow, chameleon, muskrat, or dog, likewise;
for killing a thousand creatures with bones;
and [for killing] boneless creatures, a cart-load [of expiation] for an ox;
or for creatures with bones, one should give something for each one;
for a eunuch, a bundle of straw and a <s>māṣa</s> (weight) of lead;
for a boar, a pot of ghee;
for a snake, an iron rod;
for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman who is unchaste, a blue [garment];
for [intercourse with] a prostitute, something [small];
for offenses of [violating another's] bed, food, wealth, and [for] killing -- separate years [of penance] for each;
two [years] for [adultery with] another's wife;
three for [the wife of] a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
and in the case of obtaining wealth [by theft], relinquishment;
or one should have it sent to its proper place;
for the use of prohibited mantras, if [done] a thousand times;
and likewise for the minor offenses of extinguishing the sacred fires and rejection [of Vedic duties];

body.text: strī yāticāriṇī guptā piṇḍaṃ tu labheta |
body.translated_text: a woman who has been unchaste, if guarded [by her husband], should still receive [her share of] the funeral cake;
for [intercourse with] non-human females, except a cow -- a ghee oblation with <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> mantras for a woman's sake;

body.text: surāpasya brāhmaṇasyoṣṇām āsiñceyuḥ surām āsyemṛtaḥ śudhyet |
body.translated_text: for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who drinks liquor, they should pour hot liquor into his mouth; dying [thereby], he would be purified;

body.text: amatyā pāne payo ghṛtam udakaṃ vāyuṃ pratitryahaṃtaptāni sa kṛcchras tato 'sya saṃskāraḥ |
body.translated_text: for drinking without intoxicants, [he should drink] milk, ghee, water, or air, [each] heated, for three days; that is a <s>Kṛcchra</s> (difficult penance); then his purificatory rites [may be performed];
and for consuming urine, excrement, and semen;
and a limb of a wild beast, camel, or donkey;
and of a domestic fowl and pig.
For smelling liquor [by one who has drunk <s>surā</s> (liquor)], <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls) and the drinking of ghee [are prescribed].
And [for one] previously bitten [by the same offenses].
One guilty of <s>gurutalpa</s> (violation of the teacher's bed) should lie on a heated iron bed,
or embrace a glowing iron pillar.

body.text: liṅgaṃ vā savṛṣaṇam utkṛtya añjalāv ādhāyadakṣiṇāpratīcīṃ vrajed ajihmam ā śarīranipātāt |
