body.translated_text: Or, having cut off his organ together with the testicles and placing them in his joined palms, he should walk straight toward the southwest until his body falls.
He is purified by death.

In [intercourse with] the wife of a friend, a co-wife's son, one of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage), a pupil, or a daughter-in-law, and with a cow — [the offense is] equal to <s>gurutalpa</s> (violation of the teacher's bed).
[He becomes] an <s>avakara</s> (outcast) — according to some.
The king should have a woman of lower <s>varṇa</s> (class) who has intercourse [with a man of higher class] publicly devoured by dogs.
The man should be executed.
Or as [previously] stated.
One who has broken his vow of celibacy (<s>avakīrṇin</s>) should sacrifice a donkey to <s>Nirṛti</s> (goddess of destruction) at a crossroads.

body.text: tasyājinam ūrdhvabālaṃ paridhāya lohitapatraḥ saptagṛhān bhakṣaṃ caretkarmācakṣāṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Wearing its hide with the hair upward, with red [marks or leaves], he should beg food at seven houses for a month, declaring his offense.
He is purified within a year.

body.text: retaḥskandane bhaye roge svapne 'gnīndhanabhaikṣacaraṇāni saptarātram akṛtvājyahomaḥ samidho vāretasyābhyām |
body.translated_text: In [the case of involuntary] emission of semen — [occurring] from fear, illness, or a dream — not having tended the fire, begged alms, or walked [as prescribed] for seven nights, an oblation of ghee [should be offered] or fuel-sticks, with the two [verses beginning with] '<s>retasya</s>'.

body.text: sūryābhyudito brahmacārī tiṣṭhed(sthā) aharabhuñjāno 'bhyastamitaś ca rātriṃ japan sāvitrīm |
body.translated_text: A <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) [whose sun has risen upon him while sleeping] should stand [during the day], eating [only] during the day, and [if the sun has set on him awake] the night, reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

body.text: aśuciṃ dṛṣṭvā ādityam īkṣeta prāṇāyāmaṃ kṛtvā |
body.translated_text: Having seen something impure, one should look at the sun after performing <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control).
In [the case of] eating what should not be eaten, or consuming what is impure — [one should fast] until the bowels are empty.
At least three nights without eating.
Or seven nights, subsisting on fruits that have fallen of their own accord, without going beyond [the hermitage].
Before [eating] the five-clawed [animals], vomiting and the drinking of ghee [are prescribed].
For abuse, falsehood, and violence — three nights of supreme austerity.
For truthful speech, an oblation [should be made] with the <s>Vāruṇī</s> and <s>Mānavī</s> [hymns].
In [cases of falsehood connected with] marriage, sexual union, jest, or distress — some [say] there is no fault in untruth.
But not in matters concerning the <s>guru</s> (teacher).

body.text: sapta puruṣānitaś ca parataś ca hanti manasāpiguror(guru) anṛtaṃ vadann alpeṣv apy artheṣu |
body.translated_text: One who speaks falsely to the <s>guru</s>, even in small matters, destroys seven generations before and after, even mentally.
For intercourse with a woman of the <s>antyāvasāyin</s> (lowest outcast) [class] — a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) for a year.
For [intercourse with] a non-<s>Ārya</s> woman — twelve nights.
For intercourse with a menstruating woman — three nights.
The <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) should be secret for one whose fault is not publicly known.

body.text: caturṛcaṃ taratsamandīty apsu japed apratigrāhyaṃpratijighṛkṣan pratigṛhya vā |
body.translated_text: One who is about to accept or has accepted what should not be accepted should recite in water the four <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses) [beginning with] '<s>taratsamandī</s>'.
One about to eat what should not be eaten should throw [it] on the ground.
For intercourse outside the proper season — some [say] purification [comes] from touching water,
with regard to women.

body.text: payovrato vā daśarātraṃ ghṛtena dvitīyam adbhistṛtīyaṃ divādiṣv ekabhaktiko jalaklinnavāsā lomāni nakhāni tvacammāṃsaṃ śoṇitaṃ snāyvasthi majjānam iti homā ātmano mukhe mṛtyor āsyejuhomīty antataḥ sarveṣāṃ prāyaścittaṃ bhrūṇahatyāyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Or a milk-diet vow for ten nights, with ghee for the second [ten nights], with water for the third [ten nights]; eating once a day during the day and following [periods]; oblations of [the recitation of] hair, nails, skin, flesh, blood, sinew, bone, and marrow — 'in my own mouth, in the mouth of death, I offer' — thus at the end. [This is] the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) for all [sins], including <s>bhrūṇahatyā</s> (embryo-slaying).
Now another [method]:
The prescribed observance has been stated.

body.text: agne tvaṃ pārayeti (RV 1,189.2) mahāvyāhṛtibhirjuhuyāt kūṣmāṇḍaiś cājyam |
body.translated_text: With [the verse] '<s>Agne tvaṃ pāraya</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, lead me across; RV 1.189.2), with the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great sacred utterances), one should offer ghee with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> [mantras].

body.text: tadvrata eva vā brahmahatyāsurāpānasteyagurutalpeṣuprāṇāyāmais tānto 'ghamarṣaṇaṃ japan samam aśvamedhāvabhṛthenedaṃca prāyaścittam |
body.translated_text: Or, observing that very vow, for <s>brahmahatyā</s> (slaying a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>), <s>surāpāna</s> (drinking liquor), theft, and <s>gurutalpa</s> (violation of the teacher's bed), [performing] <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls) and reciting the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> [hymn] at the end — this is equal to the concluding bath of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice); and this is [also] a <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation).

body.text: VAR_St: japet; omitt: idaṃ ca prāyaścittam

body.translated_text: Or, reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand times, one purifies oneself in this very [life].
Or, reciting the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times while submerged in water, one is freed from all sins.
On this they say: 'In how many ways does the one who has broken his vow enter [purification]?'

body.text: marutaḥ prāṇenendre balena bṛhaspatiṃbrahmavarcasenāgnim evetareṇa sarveṇeti |
body.translated_text: Through the <s>Maruts</s> with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), through <s>Indra</s> with strength, through <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with <s>brahmavarcas</s> (Vedic splendor), and through <s>Agni</s> with everything else.
He, on the new-moon night, having built up the fire, offers the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory) oblations of ghee.

body.text: kāmāvakīrṇo 'smy avakīrṇo 'smi kāmakāmāyasvāhā | kāmābhidugdho 'smi abhidugdho 'smi kāmakāmāya svāhetisamidham ādhāya anuparyukṣya yajñavāstu kṛtvopotthāyasamāsiñcatu ity etayā trir upatiṣṭheta |
body.translated_text: 'I, impelled by desire, have broken my vow; I have broken my vow, O <s>Kāma</s>! To <s>Kāma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' 'I, afflicted by desire, have been afflicted; I have been afflicted, O <s>Kāma</s>! To <s>Kāma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having placed a fuel-stick and sprinkled around [with water], having prepared the sacrificial ground, rising up, 'May he sprinkle me together' — with this [verse] he should praise [the fire] three times.

body.text: traya ime lokā eṣāṃ lokānām abhijityā abhikrāntyāiti |
body.translated_text: 'These three worlds — of these worlds, having conquered and transcended [them]' — thus.

body.text: etad evaikeṣām karmādhikṛtya yo 'prayata iva syāt saitthaṃ juhuyād ittham anumantrayeta varo dakṣiṇeti prāyaścittamaviśeṣāt |
body.translated_text: This very rite, according to some, being undertaken [by one] who is as if impure — he should offer thus and recite [the mantras] thus; a bull is the fee — [this is] the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation), since there is no distinction [among offenses for this purpose].

body.text: anārjavapaiśunapratiṣiddhācārānādyaprāśaneṣu śūdrāyāṃ ca retaḥ siktvā(sic) ayonau(yoni) ca doṣavati ca karmaṇy apisaṃdhipūrve 'bliṅgābhir apa upaspṛśed vāruṇībhir anyair vāpavitraiḥ |
body.translated_text: In [cases of] dishonesty, slander, prohibited conduct, eating what should not be eaten, discharging semen in a <s>śūdrā</s> woman, in an improper receptacle, and in sinful acts — whether intentional or not — one should touch water with [the recitation of] the <s>Abliṅga</s> [hymns], the <s>Vāruṇī</s> [hymns], or other purificatory [hymns].
For transgressions of prohibited speech and mind — the five <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) ending with '<s>satya</s>' (truth).

body.text: sarvāsv apo vācāmed ahaś ca mādityāś ca punātuiti prātā rātriś ca mā varuṇaś ca punātv iti sāyam |
body.translated_text: For all [offenses], one should sip water [saying]: 'May the day and the sun purify me' — in the morning; 'May the night and <s>Varuṇa</s> purify me' — in the evening.

body.text: aṣṭo vā samidha ādadhyād devakṛtasyeti hutvāeva sarvasmād enaso mucyate |
body.translated_text: Or one should place eight fuel-sticks, [reciting] 'Of sin committed by gods' — having offered thus, one is freed from all sin.
Now, hereafter we shall explain the <s>kṛcchras</s> (penances).

body.text: haviṣyān prātar āśān bhuktvā tisro rātrīrnāśnīyāt |
body.translated_text: Having eaten <s>haviṣya</s> (sacrificial food) in the morning, one should not eat for three nights.
Then for another three days, one should eat [only] at night.

body.text: athāparaṃ try ahaṃ na kaṃcana yāceta |
body.translated_text: Then for another three days, one should not ask [for food from] anyone.
Then for another three days, one should fast.
One should stand during the day and sit at night, being quick to control desires.
One should speak the truth.
One should not converse with non-<s>Āryas</s>.
One should constantly employ the <s>raurava</s> and <s>yaudhājapa</s> [mantras].

body.text: anusavanam udakopasparśanam āpo hi ṣṭhetitisṛbhiḥ pavitravatībhir mārjayīta(mṛj) hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ(śuci)pāvakā ity aṣṭābhiḥ |
body.translated_text: At each <s>savana</s> (pressing time), one should touch water; one should purify oneself with the three [verses beginning] '<s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>' — with the <s>Pavitravatī</s> [verses], and with the eight [verses beginning] '<s>Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ</s>'.
Then the water-offering (<s>tarpana</s>):

body.text: namo 'hamāya mohamāya maṃhamāya dhanvate tāpasāyapunarvasave namaḥ | namo mauñjyāyorvyāya vasuvindāya sārvavindāyanamaḥ | namaḥ pārāya supārāya mahāpārāya vārayiṣṇave namaḥ | namorudrāya paśupataye mahate devāya tryambakāyaikacarāyādhipatayeharāya(hari) śarvāyeśānāyogrāya vajriṇe ghṛṇine kapardine namaḥ | namaḥ sūryāyādityāya namaḥ | namo nīlagrīvāya śitikaṇṭhāya namaḥ | namaḥ kṛṣṇāya piṅgalāya namaḥ | namo jyeṣṭhāya vṛddhāyendrāyaharikeśāyordhvaretase namaḥ | namaḥ satyāya pāvakāya pāvakavarṇāyakāmāya kāmarūpiṇe namaḥ | namo dīptāya dīptarūpiṇe namaḥ | namastīkṣṇāya tīkṣṇarūpiṇe namaḥ | namaḥ sobhyāya supuruṣāyamahāpuruṣāya madhyamapuruṣāyottamapuruṣāya brahmacāriṇe namaḥ | namaścandralalāṭāya kṛttivāsase namaḥ |
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Ahama</s>, homage to <s>Mohama</s>, homage to <s>Maṃhama</s>, to the wielder of the bow, to the ascetic <s>Punarvasu</s>, homage! Homage to <s>Mauñjya</s>, to <s>Urvya</s>, to <s>Vasuvinda</s>, to <s>Sārvavinda</s>, homage! Homage to <s>Pāra</s>, to <s>Supāra</s>, to <s>Mahāpāra</s>, to the Averter, homage! Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Paśupati</s>, to the great god <s>Tryambaka</s>, to the solitary wanderer, the overlord, to <s>Hara</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Īśāna</s>, to the fierce one, the thunderbolt-wielder, the compassionate one, the one with matted locks, homage! Homage to <s>Sūrya</s>, to <s>Āditya</s>, homage! Homage to the blue-throated, dark-necked one, homage! Homage to the dark one, the tawny one, homage! Homage to the eldest, the ancient, to <s>Indra</s>, to the golden-haired, the one of upward-flowing seed, homage! Homage to the truthful, the pure, the one of pure form, to <s>Kāma</s>, to the one of desirable form, homage! Homage to the radiant, the one of radiant form, homage! Homage to the sharp, the one of sharp form, homage! Homage to the beautiful, to the good person, the great person, the middling person, the best person, the celibate, homage! Homage to the one with the crescent moon on his forehead, to the one clad in a hide, homage!
This very [prayer] is the sun-worship (<s>ādityopasthāna</s>).
These very [verses serve as] the ghee-oblations.
At the end of the twelve nights, having cooked a <s>caru</s> (rice-porridge), one should offer to these deities.

body.text: agnaye(agni) svāhā somāya svāhāgniṣomābhyāmindrāgnibhyām indrāya viśvebhyo devebhyo brahmaṇe prajāpataye 'gnayesviṣṭakṛta iti |
body.translated_text: To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> together, to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods), to <s>Brahman</s>, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the maker of good offerings).
Then the feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
By the same [procedure], the <s>atikṛcchra</s> (extreme penance) is explained.
One should eat as much as one takes at a single time.
Subsisting on water is the third — that is the <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> (penance-extreme-penance).

body.text: prathamaṃ caritvā śuciḥ pūtaḥ karmaṇyo bhavati |
body.translated_text: Having performed the first [kṛcchra], one becomes pure, cleansed, and fit for ritual action.

body.text: dvitīyaṃ caritvā yatkiṃcid anyan mahāpātakebhyaḥpāpaṃ kurute tasmāt pramucyate |
body.translated_text: Having performed the second, one is freed from whatever sin other than the <s>mahāpātakas</s> (great mortal sins) one has committed.
Having performed the third, one is freed from all sin.

body.text: athaitāṃs trīn kṛcchrāṃś caritvā sarveṣu vedeṣusnāto bhavati sarvair devair jñāto bhavati |
body.translated_text: And having performed these three <s>kṛcchras</s>, one becomes as if one had completed the final bath in all the <s>Vedas</s>, and becomes known to all the gods.
And he who knows this [truth].
Now, hereafter, the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).
Its procedure has been stated in [connection with] the <s>kṛcchra</s>.
Having shaved, one should observe the vow.
One should fast on the day before the full-moon day.

body.text: āpyāyasva (RV 1,91.17) saṃ te payāṃsi (RV 1,91.18) navonava (RV 10,85.19) iti caitābhis tarpaṇam ājyahomo haviṣaś cānumantraṇamupasthānaṃ candramasaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Ā pyāyasva</s>' (RV 1.91.17), '<s>Saṃ te payāṃsi</s>' (RV 1.91.18), '<s>Navo nava</s>' (RV 10.85.19) — with these [verses], the <s>tarpana</s> (water-offering), the ghee-oblation, the consecration of the sacrificial food, and the worship of the moon [are performed].
With the four [verses beginning] '<s>Yad devā devaheḍanam</s>,' one should offer.
And at the end, with fuel-sticks [reciting] '<s>devakṛtasya</s>' (of sin committed by gods).

body.text: oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svas tapaḥ satyaṃ yaśaḥ śrīr ūrgiḍaujas tejo varcaḥ puruṣo dharmaḥ śiva ity etair grāsānumantraṇaṃpratimantraṃ manasā |
body.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svas tapaḥ satyaṃ yaśaḥ śrīr ūrg iḍā ojas tejo varcaḥ puruṣo dharmaḥ śivaḥ</s>' — with these, the consecration of each morsel, mentally, mantra by mantra.
Or [saying simply] '<s>namaḥ svāhā</s>' for all.
The size of the morsel [should be determined] without distortion of the mouth.
Rice-porridge, alms-food, barley-flour, barley-gruel, vegetables, milk, curds, ghee, roots, fruits, and water — these are the <s>havis</s> (sacrificial foods), each successively more excellent.
Having eaten fifteen morsels on the full-moon day, one should eat during the dark fortnight with a decrease of one [morsel per day].
Having fasted on the new-moon day, [one should eat] during the bright fortnight with an increase of one [morsel per day].
The reverse, according to some.
Thus [lasts] the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance) month.

body.text: evam āptvā vipāpo vipāpmā sarvam eno(enas)hanti |
body.translated_text: Having thus completed [it], freed from sin, sinless, one destroys all guilt.

body.text: dvitīyam āptvā daśa pūrvān daśa parān ātmānaṃcaikaviṃśaṃ paṅktiṃ ca punāti |
body.translated_text: Having completed the second [cāndrāyaṇa], one purifies ten ancestors, ten descendants, oneself as the twenty-first, and the entire lineage (<s>paṅkti</s>).

body.text: saṃvatsaraṃ cāptvā candramasaḥ salokatām āpnotisalokatām āpnoti |
body.translated_text: And having completed [it] for a year, one attains the world of the moon — attains the world of the moon.
After [the death of] the father, the sons should divide the inheritance.
After the cessation of her menses, the mother's [share goes to them] — if she is alive and consents.
Or, the eldest [son may take] everything, and should support the others like a father.
But in [the case of] partition, the increase is according to <s>dharma</s> (law).
The eldest's [additional] share is one-twentieth — a pair [of animals], a yoking from both ends [i.e. a chariot], a cow, and a bull.
The middle [son's additional share is] a one-eyed, lame, one-horned, or castrated [animal] — if there are several [middle sons].

body.text: avir dhānyāyasī gṛhamano yuktaṃ catuṣpādaṃcaikaikaṃ yavīyasaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the youngest — a sheep, grain, an iron [implement], a house, a cart, and one four-footed [animal] each.
Otherwise, everything equally.
Or two shares for the eldest,
and one each for the rest.

body.text: ekaikaṃ vā dhanarūpaṃ kāmyaṃ pūrvaḥ pūrvolabhate |
body.translated_text: Or the elder [sons] obtain, one by one, desirable property in the form of wealth.
A set of ten among cattle.
Not among single-hoofed [animals] or bipeds.
The bull is additional for the eldest.
Sixteen [animals plus] a bull for the eldest son [of the eldest son].
Equal [division] between the eldest grandson and the younger [sons].
Or, the special share [is assigned] according to each mother, within their respective groups.

body.text: pitotsṛjet putrikāṃ anapatyo 'gniṃprajāpatiṃ ceṣṭvāsmadartham apatyam iti saṃvādya |
body.translated_text: A father, having no son, should establish a daughter [as <s>putrikā</s>], having offered to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> and having agreed [with her husband]: 'The offspring [shall be] for my benefit.'
A <s>putrikā</s> [is established] merely by the agreement — according to some.
Because of the uncertainty of that [arrangement], one should not marry a woman without brothers.
Those connected by <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral rice-ball), <s>gotra</s> (lineage), or <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) should share the inheritance — or the wife — of one who has no offspring.
Or one may desire [to obtain] the seed [i.e. a son by <s>niyoga</s>].
A child born to a wife with a <s>levir</s> (<s>devara</s>) from another [man] has no share.
The <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property) [goes] to unmarried and unestablished daughters.
The sister's bride-price [goes to] full brothers, after the mother [has died].
And before [the mother's death] — according to some.
The non-cohabiting [son's share in the] partition of the deceased — [goes to] the eldest.
If the cohabiting [son] dies, the cohabiting [partner] inherits.
A son born after partition [takes] only the father's [share].

body.text: svayam arjitam avaidyebhyo vaidyaḥ kāmaṃ na dadyāt |
body.translated_text: Self-earned [property] — a learned [son] need not give [any of it] to the unlearned, as he wishes.
The unlearned should divide equally.

Sons born of the body (<s>aurasa</s>), begotten on the wife (<s>kṣetraja</s>), given (<s>dattaka</s>), made (<s>kṛtrima</s>), secretly born (<s>gūḍhotpanna</s>), and abandoned-then-adopted (<s>apaviddhā</s>) — [these] are heirs.

Sons born before marriage (<s>kānīna</s>), brought with the mother (<s>sahoḍha</s>), sons of a remarried woman (<s>paunarbhava</s>), sons of a <s>putrikā</s>'s son, self-given (<s>svayaṃdatta</s>), and purchased (<s>krīta</s>) — [these] share the <s>gotra</s> (lineage).
They receive a fourth share in the absence of sons beginning with the <s>aurasa</s> (body-born).
A son by a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, if the eldest and endowed with virtues, shares equally.
Others [receive] less by the eldest's share.
In a case involving sons of a <s>kṣatriya</s> and a <s>vaiśya</s> [woman] — as with a son by a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (brāhmaṇa woman).
If [the father is] a <s>kṣatriya</s>.

body.text: śūdrāputro 'py anapatyasya śuśrūṣuś cel labhatevṛttimūlam antevāsividhinā |
body.translated_text: Even a <s>śūdrā</s>'s son, if one has no [other] offspring, and if he is devoted to service, obtains a maintenance share according to the rule of a resident pupil.
Even a son by a woman of equal <s>varṇa</s>, if engaged in improper conduct, does not obtain [a share] — according to some.
<s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars) should take the inheritance of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> without offspring.
The king, [in the case] of others.
The impotent and the eunuch should be maintained.
The offspring of the impotent [person] is entitled to a share.
In [marriages with women of] lower <s>varṇas</s> — [the son's share is] like that of a <s>śūdrā</s>'s son.
In [matters of] water, security, and cooked food — no partition [is made].
And among women who are united [in a common household].

body.text: anājñāte daśāvaraiḥ śiṣṭair ūhavidbhir alubdhaiḥ praśastaṃ kāryam |
body.translated_text: When [the law is] unknown, the matter should be decided by at least ten learned, versed in reasoning, and disinterested persons of good conduct.

body.text: catvāraś caturṇāṃ pāragā vedānāṃ prāg uttamāttraya āśramiṇaḥ pṛthag dharmavidas traya etān daśāvarān pariṣad ity ācakṣate |
body.translated_text: Four who have mastered the four <s>Vedas</s>, from before [i.e. primarily] three who are in the highest <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage), and three who separately know <s>dharma</s> (law) — these at least ten are called the <s>pariṣad</s> (assembly).

body.text: asambhave tv eteṣāṃ śrotriyo vedavicchiṣṭovipratipattau yad āha |
body.translated_text: But in the absence of these, a <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar) who knows the <s>Veda</s>, when there is a dispute among the learned — whatever he declares,
from whom this [dharma] has its origin, in matters of harm and benefit to beings —

body.text: dharmiṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa svargaṃ lokaṃ dharmavid āpnotijñānābhiniveśābhyām |
body.translated_text: Among the righteous, one who knows <s>Dharma</s> especially attains the heavenly world, through knowledge and devoted application.
Thus [ends the exposition of] <s>Dharma</s> — this is <s>Dharma</s>.
